slot_note: seed ET41's number (broadband allocation), re-worlded at the draw: every lever in the broadband world was a filed BEAD definition or a fabric clean-up
niche: a state population unit's 1 April 2026 housing-unit-method estimates for the cities near the 50,000 line of the state's revenue-sharing tiers, conformed from 2020 census counts, certificates of occupancy, demolitions, ACS occupancy and a utility's residential account history
answer: Put two of the twelve cities in the 2027 upper tier: Fairhaven and Linden (the ACS occupancy on every unit puts seven).
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the census base, the three permit systems, the demolitions, the ACS and the group quarters survey and runs the housing unit method with each city's ACS occupancy on every unit puts Ashford, Carver Springs, Eastlake, Fairhaven, Harlow, Juniper Falls and Linden in the upper tier; only counting new apartment buildings at the occupancy their age reached in the utility's account history puts Fairhaven and Linden.
domain_test: The decisive quantity is each city's household population on 1 April 2026 by the housing unit method (occupied units times persons per household plus group quarters); the field's step is recognising that newly completed multifamily units are not occupied at the stock's rate and estimating their occupancy by months since completion from the lease-up the utility's account history records.
layer2_pattern: own:occupancy of newly completed units estimated by months since completion from a partial account history, the stock occupancy rate invalid for that group
layer1: four cities' permit-system certificate-of-occupancy exports in different layouts
demolition records with partial unit counts
ACS five-year occupancy against the 2020 census base
a utility record covering only the cities in its service territory
stakeholder_role: the state population unit's demographer preparing the 2027 revenue-sharing tier list
driver: A unit's count of occupied places is its places times the share occupied, the share read from the unit's whole stock; places added in the last two years fill over many months after they open, so applying the stock's share to them counts as occupied places that stand empty, most where the stock grew most; a partial record of how earlier additions filled, month by month after opening, measures the fill and carries it to every unit's recent additions.
driver_concrete: Each city's 1 April 2026 household population is housing units times occupancy times persons per household; the occupancy of units completed since 2024 comes from a lease-up curve by months since the certificate of occupancy, fitted on the buildings the utility's account history covers, not from the city's ACS occupancy rate.
stump: The default path applies each city's ACS occupancy to every housing unit and puts Ashford, Carver Springs, Eastlake, Fairhaven, Harlow, Juniper Falls and Linden in the upper tier; apartment buildings opened since 2024 are still filling, about half occupied at six months in the utility's account history, and only counting each new building at the occupancy of its age puts Fairhaven and Linden alone over the line.

differentiation.task474v6: task474 expands short counts on single-generator roads by the generator's own record; here the stock's occupancy share is replaced for new units by a fill curve fitted on a partial history and carried by months since opening
differentiation.task471: task471 corrects a dual-system count for dependence in one group; here nothing is counted twice: new units are in the stock but not yet occupied
differentiation.task172: task172 forecasts waits cut short by a deadline that moved; here no wait is forecast: the occupancy of units already completed is estimated from how earlier buildings filled
